chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever is just in his bequest is like the one who gave it in charity during his lifetime; and whoever is inequitable in his bequest will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, and He will turn away from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for being just in one's will or bequest according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the execution of a fair will (wasiyyah) to the spiritual rank of voluntary charity (sadaqah), highlighting the continuity of reward after death. Conversely, it warns that injustice in bequest—often linked to favoritism among heirs—results in divine alienation (mu'rid), emphasizing that equitable distribution is a key criterion for Allah's pleasure on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘The one who does justice in his bequest would be at the status of the one who gave in charity with it during his lifetime; and the one who is inequitable in his bequest would meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic on the Day of Judgement, and He<sup>azwj</sup> would Turn away from him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One who maintains justice in his will is like one who has given in charity in his lifetime and one who is unjust in his will he, on the Day of Judgment, will come before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, who will shun him.’”
